evidence.ref: The two-key freshness helper _expired (.warp/two_key.py), the single freshness check authorize() applies to BOTH keys, now FAILS CLOSED when no clock is available. Before, the no-clock branch returned False (fresh) for a key that DECLARES an expiry even a PAST one, so an expired-but-declared key passed. After, that branch returns True (expired); because the no-declared-expiry branch already returned True, _expired is now False (fresh) ONLY when a real clock (now) proves a declared expiry lies in the future - every other case (no expiry, or a declared expiry unverifiable for want of a clock) is expired and the gate REFUSES by name (authorization_expired / confirmation_expired). Minimal and surgical: only the no-clock branch changes (return False -> return True) plus its docstring and the two refusal-detail strings; no other guard, the two-distinct-keys guarantee, the digest binding, the self-separation, or the L2 single-confirmation path is touched. python3 .warp/two_key.py still AUTHORIZES the demo pair (it injects a clock) and --one-key still REFUSES (missing_independent_confirmation).
